newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK January retail price data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK January retail price data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK data showing retail prices gained 2.8 percent y/y versus 2.5 percent previously. RPIX up 3.1 percent y/y versus 3.1 previously.
"The headline number of 3.1 percent is somewhat higher than expected."
"This gives a little more credence to the Bank of England's view that we should see a small tightening in monetary policy in the near furture."

"In terms of the targetting measure, the RPIX has come in a little worse than expected. The market wasn't really factoring in enough of a rise in seasonal food prices which have risen fairly sharply due to the cold weather over the winter."
"The other main factor are petrol, oil and motoring costs, which have not fallen as mush as expected."
"I'm still thinking that the underlying rate should nudge a little bit lower in the next few months, but it is touch and go whether we move back to the government's rate."

"It is quite clear from Mr Clarke's comments that he is not going to raise rates ahead of the election. But in the run-up to the election, the market are going to become a bit nervous. We may have some of the best news for the gilt market behind us."

"The breakdown of the RPIX is much weaker than an unchanged annual rate would imply. Most of the key categories show significant declines, notably the clothing and footwear sector, which in recent months has seen price hikes."

"But for bad weather effects on food -- always the risk -- underlying inflation would have fallen. Data should be seen as supportive of the Chancellor's refusal to hike rates and should help to ease any inflation worries triggered by the jump in earnings growth reported yesterday. Indeed the weakness of the breakdown must be positive for near-term inflation prospects."

"Higher housing costs were the main factor for the RPI in January, as expected. Yearly rate of underlying inflation is due to offsetting effects of higher seasonal food and lower clothing and footwear prices."

"Maintains view that government will not achieve its inflation target even in the short term. Neutral to slightly negative for gilts and sterling. Of no importance for base rates in next couple of months, which we all know will remain flat until the election."
